title: Split a full name for a CRM that wants two fields
examObjective: Applying correct syntax to write DataWeave transformations to coerce, format, order, and filter data
basics: `splitBy` cuts a String into an Array of pieces wherever a separator appears: `"a b" splitBy " "` gives `["a", "b"]`. The separator can be a String or a regular expression written between slashes, such as `/\s+/` for "one or more whitespace characters".
prompt:
The old CRM stored one `fullName` field. The new one wants `first` and `last`.

For each customer, `first` is the first word of the name and `last` is the last word. Middle names are dropped. A customer with a one-word name has `last: null`.

The names were typed by hand, so there may be extra spaces anywhere: before, after, or several between words.
hints: Split the name into words, then take the first and the last one. Negative indexes count from the end.
What does `"  Alan   Turing " splitBy " "` return? Try it.
Trim first, and split on a regex that matches any run of whitespace: `/\s+/`. For a single word, check the number of parts.

mustFail.why: splits on a single space, so extra spaces produce empty pieces and the first or last word comes out as ""
takes the last word unconditionally, so a one-word name gets the same word as first and last

explanation.approach: Splitting on one space keeps every empty piece between two spaces, and the leading spaces make the very first piece empty. Trimming and splitting on a whitespace regex gives clean words. The one-word case needs its own check, because `[-1]` on a one-element array is that same element.

snippets.label: Splitting on a single space
snippets.note: Every gap between two spaces becomes an empty String.

snippets.label: Trim, then split on a regex
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
trim("  Alan   Turing ") splitBy /\s+/

snippets.label: The last word of a one-word name
snippets.note: The first word and the last word are the same element.
